long_biography.plain_text:
Abraham Cababie Daniel began by arranging international franchise agreements for his family's textile enterprise. Mexico's trade liberalisation altered that industry's prospects, and in 1989 he joined brothers Elías and Jacobo in moving into property development. Their new business became GICSA.

Cababie took the chief-executive role while Elías chaired the board, a division of responsibility that continues. GICSA expanded across shopping centres, offices, mixed-use complexes, industrial space, housing and hospitality before listing shares publicly. Abraham also serves as board vice-chairman. The Cababie Daniel family and related parties held 57.27 per cent of the company in 2024. No individual percentage was allocated to Abraham. His co-founding, executive work and family ownership support real estate as both the source and current focus of his wealth. GICSA's properties, investment budgets, debt and market value remain corporate measures rather than his personal assets.

GICSA's properties, investment budgets, debt and market value remain corporate measures rather than his personal assets.
